messages:
samira_support: Hey team — my April payslip shows FICA and Federal withholding. Im a Spain-based employee (Madrid) on local payroll. I uploaded my NIE and residency docs in Jan. Why is US payroll withholding on my pay?

olga_payroll: Yikes, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the redacted stub lines? Also did you ever have US citizenship flagged in ADP/Workday? That can flip the payroll channel.

samira_support: Stub lines (redacted):

```
Pay date: 04/30/2026
Gross EUR: 5,200.00
IRPF (Spain): 1,248.00
Social Security (Spain): 425.00
Federal tax (US): 780.00
FICA: 398.00
Net EUR: 2,349.00
```

dan_hr: I checked HRIS — home country=ES, docs present. However the foreign passport field had dual nationality flagged (US) from onboarding and the US-citizenship box was ticked by mistake. That flag routes you to US payroll for one run. I'll clear the US flag immediately.

matt_finance: Operational note: if US FICA/federal were included and remitted, reversal depends on remittance timing and whether funds left the US processor. Also cross-border payrolls require correct tax treaty handling; Spain-US treaty generally exempts some items but FICA can be sticky depending on Social Security Totalization Agreement. We need to confirm whether the amounts were remitted.

payroll-bot: Payroll run 2026-04-30 processed. Batch id pr-20260430-4412. Outgoing remittance to US processor initiated 2026-05-01 02:14 UTC.

olga_payroll: Seems like remittance was initiated. Next steps: (1) We'll request a stop/reclaim with the US payment processor ASAP (ticket PAY-INTL-5058). (2) If reclaim succeeds, we'll post an off-cycle reversal and correct Spanish payroll entries. (3) If reclaim fails, we'll coordinate with Finance and Tax counsel about refund paths (employer reclaim vs. employee IRS filing).

samira_support: If it comes down to me filing with the IRS, what forms would I need? I don't want to be on the hook for employer-side mistakes.

matt_finance: If funds were remitted and can't be recovered, the employee may need a refund claim via Form 843 (claim for refund) or reclassification paperwork. But typically employer-paid FICA withheld in error is corrected by employer and W-2 amended (W-2c) so employee isn't out of pocket. We'll push to recover before that.

dan_hr: I've cleared the US citizenship flag and added a note showing your Spain residency effective 2024-07-01. Also, Samira, please confirm your social security certificate if you have a Spanish Social Security number so payroll can ensure proper SS mapping.

olga_payroll: Submitted PAY-INTL-5058 to payment ops (estimated response 3 business days). If reclaim confirmed, off-cycle reversal target within 7 business days. I'll attach a provisional stub to the ticket showing the reversal line: "Correction: US withholding reversal (period 04/30/2026)".

samira_support: Thanks. One more Q: will this affect year-end forms? I'm worried about receiving a W-2 or a hybrid notice.

matt_finance: Good question. If the record was processed on US payroll files we might temporarily have a US wage record. If we successfully reverse before W-2 preparation, there should be no W-2. If not, we'll issue a corrected W-2 (W-2c) and coordinate to ensure Spanish T4-equivalent reporting is accurate. We'll also involve external tax counsel to confirm treaty treatment.

olga_payroll: I'll post updates here and on PAY-INTL-5058. Samira — you don't need to take immediate action unless we ask you to sign a confirmation. We'll aim to keep any required employee action minimal. :thumbsup:

payroll-bot: PAY-INTL-5058 created and assigned to olga_payroll. Estimated resolution: 2026-05-10.
